paragraphs: Miss your familiar extension cords when you switch from power tools to digital gadgets? Now you don’t have to. The Extension-C looks like a regular power cable, but it has USB-C connectors on each end rather than power prongs.

It was designed by Matty Benedetto, the creator of Unnecessary Inventions. It’s kind of a joke, but quite useful, too. It really can power your devices and run your accessories. And it’s 10 feet long!
I ran the Extension-C through testing — here’s why I think it makes a great gift.

My father grew up on a farm then ran a construction company. To say that he entered the digital age with reluctance is putting it mildly. He’s far more likely to use a jigsaw than Facebook. But he can’t escape the online world.

That’s why he’s getting an Extension-C for Christmas. I’m sure he’ll get a laugh from using what looks like an extension cord to power up his phone. So, does my dad sound like someone on your gift list?

Extension-C gives the charging cable a little more personality by borrowing from something instantly familiar: the classic extension cord. The chunky molded ends, the ridged details, the unmistakable plug shape — all reimagined as a USB-C to USB-C charging cable.
When you need to run power tools, you grab an extension cord out of the garage or workshop. It’s bright orange with a heavy plug on each end.
When you need to charge your iPhone or MacBook, you can grab an Extension-C. It’s also bright orange with a heavy plug on each end. (There are also green and black versions)
